subject: [COMPANY] & Encord - Intro
text:
Hi [NAME],

I was reading about the curbside optimization you're leading in SF
(heartfelt thank you for making my way to work easier!) Thought I'd reach
out since we work with Automotus & AGD Systems on developing very similar
predictive ML models for curb management, with the goals to speed up new
transport analytics product releases.

We're mostly assisting with improving model quality / delivery speed while
keeping development costs low as they scale through better end-to-end data
mgmt and by allowing them to curate/annotate data from connected vehicles
at scale on our platform.

Bit of context on Encord: we're a data development platform built for
advanced computer vision and multimodal AI teams to build better models (~5
years old, 90+ employees & raised $50M+ funding).

I've been following [COMPANY] for a while now and get your candid feedback on
what we're building here at Encord if you have 30mins to chat. Open to a
quick call this week or the next? Wednesdays / Thursdays work best for me.

subject: Skeleton tracking at [COMPANY] | Working with Hudl & Pixellot
text:
Hi [NAME]​,

I've been following [COMPANY]'s recent expansion post-EA acquisition and your deep-learning work powering skeleton tracking from 25-60 Hz video streams. Given the precision demands of your CV models (e.g. 21-joint pose estimation, offside line detection), I imagine managing labeled data at scale is becoming increasingly complex.

At Encord, we've been working with CV sports analytics teams (Hudl, Pixellot, Veo, Spiideo) to centralize annotation workflows, integrate human-in-the-loop QA, surface edge cases, and automate large-scale labeling through techniques like active learning and ontology-driven labeling. 

Open to a quick 20-min chat next week? Would love to hear how you're approaching this at [COMPANY].

subject: Improving Perception Data
text:
Hi [NAME],

We've been working with perception teams like 1X Robotics, Boston Dynamics,
and Toyota by Woven to help them leverage the data their robots generate in
production.

As microfactory deployments expand, you'll naturally see more edge cases,
SKU changes, and environment variability. The teams scaling fastest are the
ones treating this real-world data as an asset, not a bottleneck.

Encord centralizes production data, makes it searchable, and provides
pre-labeling + evaluation workflows so your perception models can adapt
faster to new products and conditions without slowing down engineering
velocity.

Would you be open to a quick conversation? Just let me know what works best
for you

-[SENDER]
